{
  "hypothesis": "Predicted that the intervention group would improve their time until the first hit in shoot scenarios to a greater extent than the control group.",
  "design": "mixed, 2 (group: intervention vs. control) x 2 (measurement time: pre-test vs. post-test)",
  "manipulation_or_predictor": "An individual video-based firearms training intervention based on the Four-Component Instructional Design Model (4C/ID), focusing on situational awareness, tactical gaze control, and visual attention, compared to an active control training resembling traditional police firearms training.",
  "outcome_measure": "Time until the first hit (in milliseconds) in realistic shoot/don't shoot video scenarios, measured as the time between the detection of the black handgun and the first effective hit in predefined areas.",
  "population_and_setting": "45 senior police officers recruited from the German Police University, tested in an indoor firing range lab setting.",
  "sample_size_total": 45,
  "recruitment_and_incentive": "Recruited via notices on campus; participation was voluntary.",
  "analysis_plan": "Repeated measures ANOVA with the within-subject factor Time and the between-subject factor Group.",
  "preregistered_or_confirmatory": "preregistered",
  "other_methods_notes": "Participants used a gas-operated replica of a Heckler and Koch SFP9 handgun. The study included a pre-test, a training phase, and a post-test. Participants were excluded if they wore glasses or if they did not hit the predefined areas in at least one shoot scenario."
